column1: # Sudan, the Fiqh Academy: Khartoum State's Ministry of Religious Affairs and Endowments imsakiya for
# Ramadan 1443 (2022, UTC+2), the one table held (profiles-tested.md, authorities-arab-world-turkiye.md),
# at the research's Khartoum point. Africa/Khartoum. Standard Asr. Its first column, labelled imsak,
# is the Fajr and when the fast begins (the Academy calls an imsak before Fajr unfounded): F+E. No
# One table: fit, nothing held out.
# Not a row: nile/khartoum.txt, eight days of Ramadan 2026 from agentB/sudan1.json ("Khartoum Fiqh
# Academy Ramadan 2026"), which gives no source. It looks like an Umm al-Qura-style calculator's
# output: columns named noon and sunset, Fajr near 18.6°, Isha = Maghrib + 90 on all eight days
# without Umm al-Qura's Ramadan 120. It is not taken as the Academy's table until a source is found.
# Ruling R74: a second, independent republication (a Sudanese news aggregator's Ramadan 2026
# imsakiya, attributed to the Fiqh Academy) gives the same day-1 Khartoum Fajr and Isha as
# nile/khartoum.txt, so the Maghrib + 90 figure is no longer an isolated data point, though its
# authorship is still unconfirmed. sd.ministry now carries a Ramadan-only Isha floor (Maghrib + 90,
# never earlier than the 18.0° angle) as a safety margin against it; this table's own Isha, which
# fits the 18.0° angle exactly, is up to 20 min "late" against that floor on its own Ramadan
# 1443 dates (a recorded exception, not an error: the floor only ever moves Isha later).

column6: F+E S D A M I
